questions.prompt: Module app.handlers does `from app.services import send_email`. Which patch target is correct?
questions.explanation: Patch where the name is looked up — handlers imported its own reference, so you must replace app.handlers.send_email, not the definition site.

questions.prompt: What does autospec=True protect you from?

options.text: Mocks that silently accept misspelled attributes and wrong-signature calls

questions.explanation: autospec builds the double from the real API, so wrong names and bad call signatures raise instead of passing silently.

questions.prompt: The golden rule of patching: patch where the name is ____ ____, not where it is defined.
questions.explanation: You must replace the reference in the module that uses the name, because Python bound that reference at import time.

questions.prompt: Which are good mocking practices? Select all that apply.

options.text: Use autospec=True so typos and bad signatures fail loudly
Wrap third-party services in your own adapter and double that boundary
Patch the definition site so the change is global and permanent
Let patch/monkeypatch automatically undo the replacement

questions.explanation: Autospec, owning the boundary, and auto-undo are all sound; patching the definition site (and leaving globals replaced) is the mistake.

questions.prompt: Match each tool to what it does.

pairs.right: Temporarily replace a dotted name, then restore it
Patch a specific attribute of an object/class
Build the mock from the real API to catch bad calls
pytest fixture to set/replace attrs and env vars, auto-undone

questions.explanation: These are the core patching tools; each replaces something temporarily, and autospec keeps the double faithful.

questions.prompt: Order the steps to correctly patch a dependency used inside a function.

items.text: Find which module looks up the name
Patch that module's name with autospec=True
Configure the return/side_effect and assert behavior

questions.explanation: Identify the lookup site, patch it faithfully with autospec, then drive and verify the test.
